newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS NAME PAT BURNS HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS NAME PAT BURNS HEAD COACH.

text.p: The Boston Bruins, whose string of 29 consecutive playoff appearances was snapped this season, on Wednesday named Pat Burns as their new head coach.
Burns, who became the fifth head coach for Boston in the last eight years, replaces Steve Kasper, who was fired last month after two seasons behind the Bruins' bench.
Boston finished last in the Northeast Division to end a playoff streak that had been the longest in professional sports.
The 45-year-old Burns, a retired police officer, has been out of hockey since he was fired by the Toronto Maple Leafs in March 1996.
One of only two coaches who have won the Jack Adams Award as coach of the year with two different teams, Burns owns a career coaching mark of 307-211-83 with the Montreal Canadiens and Toronto.

He won his first Adams Award in 1988-89 after guiding the Canadiens to a 53-18-9 record and a berth in the Stanley Cup Finals in his first year behind the bench. Montreal never finished worse than nine games over .500 in four years under Burns, who jumped to Toronto before the 1992-93 season.

In Burns's first season with Toronto, the Maple Leafs set club records for wins (44), points (99), home wins (25), and playoff victories (11) and reached the conference finals as Burns claimed coach of the year honours again.
